title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: Guess: an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high‐entropy alloy (HEA) homogenized and solution‐treated
recollection.intervention: Guess: isothermal aging at ~600 °C for various times (0, 100, 500, 1000 h)
recollection.structure: Guess: fine intermetallic precipitates (σ‐phase or L12‐type) nucleating at grain boundaries and within grains at intermediate aging times, coarsening into larger, more stable particles after prolonged aging
recollection.mechanism: Guess: initial ductility loss due to embrittling precipitate formation and grain‐boundary segregation, followed by coarsening that reduces precipitate number density and relaxes internal stresses, restoring ductility
recollection.results: Guess: room‐temperature fracture toughness K_IC falls from ≈100 MPa√m (as‐quenched) to ≈45 MPa√m after ~500 h, then recovers to ≈80 MPa√m after ~1000 h; tensile elongation drops from ≈60% to ≈8% at peak embrittlement and rebounds to ≈40% on overaging

score.note: The recollection correctly guesses aging near 600°C but incorrectly frames the transition as time-dependent overaging and omits the ~750°C recovery treatment. It only tentatively mentions L12 precipitates while missing enhanced L12 ordering, Ni3Al-like stoichiometry, and jagged B2/FCC boundaries. The proposed coarsening/segregation mechanism is inconsistent with the reported APBE/modulus, planar-slip, boundary stress-concentration, and transition-zone mechanism. The numerical toughness and elongation values are unsupported and do not correspond to the stated results.
